==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈɹɪdəl/|[ˈɹʷɪdəl]|~|[ˈɹʷɪdl̩]}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-riddle.wav|a=Southern England}} *** {{IPA|en|/ˈɹɪɾəl/|[ˈɹʷɪɾəl]|~|[ˈɹʷɪɾl̩]|a=US,CA,t-flapping}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪdəl|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|rid|dle}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:redel|id=puzzle|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|redel}}, {{m|enm|redels}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rǣdels}}, {{m|ang|rǣdelse|t=counsel, opinion, imagination, riddle}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*rādislī|t=counsel, conjecture}}. Analyzable as {{af|en|rede|t1=advice|-le}}. Akin to {{cog|ang|rǣdan||to read, advise, interpret}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|raadsel}}, {{cog|de|Rätsel}}. ====Noun==== {{examples|: '''6th c. {{BCE}}''', Laozi, ''{{w|Tao Te Ching}}'' 9: :: Keep sharpening the blade, you'll soon blunt it. : {{RQ:King James Version|Luke|17|33}} :: Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it. |sense=ancient form}} {{en-noun}} # A [[verbal]] [[puzzle]], [[mystery]], or other [[problem]] of an [[intellectual]] nature. #: {{syn|en|enigma|conundrum|brain-teaser}} #: {{ux|en|Here's a '''riddle''': It's black, and white, and red all over. What is it?}} #* {{RQ:King James Version|Judges|14|12|14|passage=12 ¶ And Samson said vnto them, I will now put foorth a '''riddle''' vnto you: if you can certeinly declare it me, within the seuen dayes of the feast, and finde it out, then I will giue you thirtie sheetes, and thirtie change of garments:
13 But if ye cannot declare it me, then shall yee giue me thirtie sheetes, and thirtie change of garments. And they said vnto him, Put foorth thy '''riddle''', that we may heare it.
14 And hee said vnto them, Out of the eater came foorth meate, aud out of the strong came foorth sweetnesse. And they could not in three dayes expound the '''riddle'''.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Regained|book=Samson Agonistes|page=72|passage=To wring from me and tell to them my ſecret, / That ſolv'd the '''riddle''' which I had propos'd.}} #* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|VIII|passage=Elbows almost touching they leaned at ease, idly reading the almost obliterated lines engraved there. ¶ {{nowrap|"I never}} understood it," she observed, lightly scornful. "What occult meaning has a sun-dial for the spooney? ''I'm'' sure I don't want to read '''riddles''' in a strange gentleman's optics."}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1992|artist={{w|Alice in Chains|Alice in Chains}}|title={{w|Dirt (Alice in Chains album)|Rain When I Die}}|passage=I'm a '''riddle''' so strong, you can't break me}} # An ancient verbal, poetic, or literary form, in which, rather than a [[rhyme]] scheme, there are parallel opposing expressions with a hidden meaning. =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|riddlelike|riddlesome|world riddle|riddler|riddle canon|riddle wrapped in an enigma|riddle me ree|riddle me this|riddle stick}} {{clear}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|verbal puzzle}} * Afrikaans: * Ahtna: * Albanian: * Arabic: * Armenian: * Assamese: * Azerbaijani: * Bashkir: * Belarusian: * Bhojpuri: * Bulgarian: * Burmese: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Faroese: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Indonesian: * Ingrian: * Irish: * Italian: * Ivatan: * Japanese: * Kapampangan: * Kazakh: * Korean: * Kyrgyz: * Ladino: * Latin: * Latvian: * Lithuanian: * Macedonian: * Malay: * Māori: * Middle English: * Mirandese: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Pashto: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|зага́дка|f}}, {{t+|ru|ре́бус|m}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Sicilian: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Southern Altai: * Spanish: * Sundanese: * Swahili: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Tajik: * Thai: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Urdu: * Uyghur: * Uzbek: * Vietnamese: * Walloon: * Welsh: * Yakan: {{trans-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[speak]] [[ambiguously]] or [[enigmatically]]. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[solve]], [[answer]], or [[explicate]] a riddle or question. #: {{syn|en|decipher|puzzle out|unriddle|Thesaurus:solve}} #: {{ux|en|'''Riddle''' me this.}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|riddlee|unriddle|unriddleable|riddlingly}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to solve, answer, or explicate a riddle or question}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * Galician: * German: * Greek: * Italian: * Kapampangan: * Russian: {{t+|ru|разга́дывать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|разгада́ть|pf}} {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:riddil//ridelle>|id=sieve|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|riddil}}, {{m|enm|ridelle||sieve}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hriddel||sieve}}, alteration of earlier {{m|ang|hridder}}, {{m|ang|hrīder}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hrīdrā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hrīdrą}}, {{m|gem-pro|*hrīdrǭ||sieve}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hrid-||to shake}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*krey-}}. Akin to {{cog|de|Reiter||sieve}}, {{cog|non|hreinn||pure, clean}}, {{cog|goh|hreini||pure, clean}}, {{cog|got|𐌷𐍂𐌰𐌹𐌽𐍃||clean, pure}}. More at {{l|en|rinse}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|sieve}} A [[sieve]] with coarse [[mesh]]es, usually of wire, for separating coarser materials from finer, as chaff from grain, cinders from ashes, or gravel from sand. # A [[board]] with a row of [[pin]]s, set [[zigzag]], between which wire is drawn to [[straighten]] it. =====Translations===== {{trans-see|sieve}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # To put something through a [[#Noun 2|riddle]] or [[sieve#Noun|sieve]]; to [[sieve#Verb|sieve]]; to [[sift#Verb|sift]]. #: {{ux|en|You have to '''riddle''' the gravel before you lay it on the road.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|author=Helen Yemm|title=Thorny problems: How can I revive a forsythia hedge? [print version 5 April 2014, p. G9]|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/gardeningadvice/10743118/Thorny-problems-how-can-I-revive-a-forsythia-hedge.html|newspaper={{w|The Daily Telegraph}} (Gardening)|location=London|date=8 April 2014|passage=In its finest form – two years old or more – leaf mould can be '''riddled''' (sieved) and used, mixed 50/50 with sand, to make fine potting compost for seeds and cuttings.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250315055821/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/gardeningadvice/10743118/Thorny-problems-how-can-I-revive-a-forsythia-hedge.html|archivedate=15 March 2025}} # To [[fill]] with [[hole]]s like a [[#Noun 2|riddle]]. #: {{ux|en|The shots from his gun began to '''riddle''' the targets.}} # {{lb|en|figuratively}} To [[fill]] or [[spread]] [[throughout]]; to [[pervade]] (with something destructive or weakening). #: {{syn|en|litter|}} #: {{ux|en|Your argument is '''riddled''' with errors.}} #* {{RQ:Donne Devotions|chapter=1. Meditation|page=8|passage=O perplex'd diſcompoſition, O '''ridling''' diſtemper, O miſerable condition of Man.|footer=An adjective use.}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to put something through a riddle or sieve}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Greek: * Irish: * Italian: * Polish: * Russian: {{t+|ru|просеивать|impf}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to fill with holes like a riddle}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Irish: * Italian: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|изрешечивать|impf}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to fill or spread throughout; to pervade}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Irish: * Italian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|заполонять|impf}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 3=== {{ety|en|id=curtain}} {{dercat|en|gmw-pro|gem-pro}} From {{inh|en|enm|riddel}}, {{m|enm|ridel}}, {{m|enm|redel}}, {{m|enm|rudel}}, from {{der|en|fro|ridel}} {{gloss|"a plaited stuff; curtain"; > Medieval Latin {{m|la|ridellus}}}}, from {{m|fro|rider||to wrinkle}}, from {{der|en|goh|rīdan||to turn; wrap; twist; wrinkle}}. More at {{l|en|writhe}}. Doublet of {{m|en|rideau}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[curtain]]; [[bedcurtain]]. # {{lb|en|religious}} One of the pair of curtains enclosing an altar on the north and south. ===Etymology 4=== {{ety|en|id=to plait}} From {{inh|en|enm|ridlen}}, from the noun (see above). ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[plait]]. ===Further reading=== * {{pedia|riddle (disambiguation)}} * {{pedia}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=ddeilr|dreidl|lidder}}
